key_insight: AlB12–Al detonation coatings improved the wear resistance of steel 45, with AB70 exhibiting stable tribological behavior across the tested friction conditions.
engineering_relevance: These coatings offer a potential wear-resistant surface treatment for steel components exposed to sliding friction.
method: Applied AB70 (30 wt.% Al) and AB30 (70 wt.% Al) coatings using a DNEPR-5M detonation-spray installation.
Characterized coating thickness and hardness, and evaluated friction and wear under varying sliding speeds and loads.
Examined post-friction surface structures to identify wear mechanisms.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports coating thicknesses of approximately 170–200 μm and AB70 friction coefficients of 0.21–0.38 with wear rates of 3.3–8.6 μm/km; coated samples outperformed uncoated steel 45 in wear resistance.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify test loads, sliding speeds, or repeatability, limiting assessment of performance outside the tested conditions.
paper_title: Structure and properties of AlB12-Al detonation coatings on steel 45
